text:
In der Eile sind anliegende Blanquets
neulich bey Abgang der Estaffette ver¬
gessen worden; Euer Hochwohlgebohren,
werden dies Versehen gnädig verzeihen.
Ich empfehle mich Denenselben zu Gna¬
den, und wünsche, daß dieselben ver¬
gnügter als ich leben mögten; denn ich
habe in kurzer Zeit, im Herrendienste
allerley traurige Erfahrungen gemacht,
Wir alt Ingelfingen Diener werden,
über den neuern vergeßen, welche lezten
sie seyen noch so verdienstlos — dennoch glük¬
lich gemacht werden. Mich ehrlichen Teufel
wird man an der magern Angel zu tode

wollen zäppeln lassen, wo andre vom
Jette des hohenlohischen Landes schwelgen.
aber wenn das Glück mir nicht ganz no¬
unhold ist, werde ich mich aus eigener Kraff
loswinden, da man alle treue min¬
intressirte Dienste vergessen zu haben scheint.
Ich habe zu grenzenloses Vertrauen in
dieselben, als daß ich glauben konnte fünd¬
Hochwohlgebohren würden irgend von
dem Ausbruch meines Herzens Gebrauch ma¬
chen; aber etwas mußte ich dieselben
doch fühlen lassen, wie man mit mir ver¬
führt. Die treuſte Verehrung bleibt
denenselben, auf ewig gewidmet.
Ingelfingen d 15ten Maj 1806.
A: Hahn

translation.en: In the haste, the enclosed blank forms were lately forgotten upon the departure of the express courier; Your Right Honourable will graciously pardon this oversight. I commend myself to your good graces, and wish that you may live more contentedly than I; for in a short time I have had all manner of sad experiences in the service of great lords. We old Ingelfingen servants are forgotten for the sake of the newer ones, and these latter, be they ever so undeserving, are nevertheless made fortunate. Me, an honest devil, they mean to let dangle to death on the lean hook,

while others feast on the fat of the Hohenlohe lands. But if fortune is not wholly [uncertain: unfavourable] to me, I shall extricate myself by my own strength, since all faithful and disinterested services seem to have been forgotten. I have too boundless a confidence in you to be able to believe that Your Right Honourable would make any use whatever of this outpouring of my heart; but something of it I had nonetheless to let you feel, of how I am being dealt with. The most faithful reverence remains dedicated to you for ever. Ingelfingen, the 15th of May 1806. A: Hahn

text_english:
In the haste, the enclosed blank forms were lately forgotten upon the departure of the express courier; Your Right Honourable will graciously pardon this oversight. I commend myself to your good graces, and wish that you may live more contentedly than I; for in a short time I have had all manner of sad experiences in the service of great lords. We old Ingelfingen servants are forgotten for the sake of the newer ones, and these latter, be they ever so undeserving, are nevertheless made fortunate. Me, an honest devil, they mean to let dangle to death on the lean hook,

while others feast on the fat of the Hohenlohe lands. But if fortune is not wholly [uncertain: unfavourable] to me, I shall extricate myself by my own strength, since all faithful and disinterested services seem to have been forgotten. I have too boundless a confidence in you to be able to believe that Your Right Honourable would make any use whatever of this outpouring of my heart; but something of it I had nonetheless to let you feel, of how I am being dealt with. The most faithful reverence remains dedicated to you for ever. Ingelfingen, the 15th of May 1806. A: Hahn
summary_en: Hahn apologises for having forgotten to send the enclosed blank forms when the express courier left, then vents at length about his treatment in the service of great lords: old Ingelfingen servants, he complains, are forgotten in favour of undeserving newcomers who feast on the fat of the Hohenlohe lands while he is left to dangle on the lean hook. He hopes to extricate himself by his own strength and asks Triebenfeld to make no use of this confidence.
summary_de: Entschuldigt sich, daß die beiliegenden Blanquette bei der eiligen Abfertigung des Estafettenboten vergessen worden seien. Anschließend beklagt Hahn vertraulich seine Lage im Dienst großer Herren: die alten Ingelfinger Diener würden über den neueren vergessen, diese, so unverdient auch immer, glücklich gemacht, während man ihn am mageren Haken verschmachten lasse, indes andere sich vom Fett der Hohenlohischen Lande nährten. Er hoffe, sich aus eigener Kraft zu helfen, und vertraut auf Triebenfelds Verschwiegenheit.
